title: Timing it right: dephosphorylation of a key transcription factor constrains the tapetal transcriptional cascade for timely pollen development
content: Once made, some decisions are impossible to undo. For plants, the significance of certain developmental choices weighs heavily: processes like germination, flowering, and seed set must be finely timed to maximize survival. During tissue development, the need for temporal precision is apparent as new cell types must emerge at the right time and place. In pollen development, microspores are initially surrounded by the tapetum, a supporting somatic layer that secretes nutrients and components necessary for pollen grain formation. Later, the tapetum undergoes programmed cell death, releasing its final cargo of support substances, including precursors of the pollen cell wall. Timely development of the tapetum is crucial for pollen fertility, with precocious or delayed tapetal activity leading to severe sterility (Lou et al. 2018). As such, activation of the tapetal program is tightly controlled by a complex transcriptional network of feed-forward and positive feedback loops. While these reinforce the initial commitment to tapetal development, it is less understood how excessive transcriptional activation is prevented to ensure pollen wall homeostasis.
